_comment: Coverage Engine config. perFeatureArchetypes uses the canonical archetype vocabulary shared with the coverage matrix: positive | negative. globalSuites are request-wide obligations emitted once. interactionLevel/scenario* are consumed by the graph-interaction pass; curated = graph-curated edges + rule hyperedges + bounded cluster scenarios (no generic pairwise).
_globalSuitesComment: Request-wide negative obligations (not tied to any one field). NOT currently generated — the 10% negative budget is fully consumed by per-feature negatives. Retained for a future dedicated global-negative pass.
_fieldRolesComment: Default role for a SELECTED field. target = the field is a test subject and receives dedicated cases sized by its compiled coverage obligations. support = the field is injected into generated request bodies as realistic context but never becomes a dedicated test subject on its own. Supporting fields' negative obligations are still funded by the per-feature planner — the role toggle only affects positive dedicated cases. Resolution order in app.js: user toggle in the feature tree > supportPaths prefix match > supportLeaves leaf-name match > target. Keep this list CONSERVATIVE — marking a constraint-bearing field as support removes its dedicated positive coverage. This list lives here as data so it can later migrate into enrichment/ as an authored `role` field without touching code.
_ratioComment: The suite-level allocation rule. positiveShare is a GLOBAL ratio applied to the whole suite (0.9 = 90% Positive / 10% Negative) — per-feature obligation ratios no longer decide the split. combinationShare is the slice of the suite spent on multi-feature interaction cases, funded from INSIDE the positive share (so N=40 -> 36 Positive = 30 per-feature + 6 combination, and 4 Negative). The requested count N is a CEILING, not a target: the planner produces the largest suite <= N whose positive and negative halves are both fully backed by authored coverage aspects, and generating fewer than N is normal. Because the knowledge base is ~63% positive while this rule demands 90%, POSITIVE aspects are usually the binding constraint — a narrow selection yields a smaller suite. Nothing is ever invented to reach N.
_countsComment: Retained only as a floor for target features whose enrichment authored no obligations at all. The planner is obligation-driven; these are not user-facing knobs.
_scaleComment: Scale-tier mix for cases that are scale-meaningful (e.g. multi-vehicle/job interactions, combination cases). small = 1 vehicle / 1-2 jobs; medium ≈ 40% of the UI's requested counts (rounded, with sensible floors); large = the full UI counts. The scaleSensitiveRules list identifies which cross-field rules involve scenario scale (e.g. multi-depot reachability needs >1 vehicle to demonstrate). Cases tied to features with interaction obligations or any of these rules get split 40/40/20 across tiers; everything else stays small. Tier sizes auto-scale with the Scenario UI's vehicle/job inputs — no fixed numbers here.
